description: The `DRGCODES` table contains information about Diagnosis Related Groups (DRGs) assigned to hospital admissions. It provides details such as the DRG code, a description of the DRG, the type of DRG, and associated severity and mortality risks. The table links DRG information to patient identifiers (`SUBJECT_ID`) and hospital admission identifiers (`HADM_ID`). This data can be used to analyze the types of hospital cases, resource utilization, and patient outcomes associated with different DRGs.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the table.

columns.name: SUBJECT_ID
columns.description: The patient identifier.

columns.name: HADM_ID
columns.description: Hospital admission identifier. Each HADM_ID represents a unique admission to the hospital.

columns.name: DRG_TYPE
columns.description: The type of Diagnosis Related Group. DRG is a system to classify hospital cases into one of several groups, with similar clinical conditions requiring similar resource usage.

columns.name: DRG_CODE
columns.description: Numeric code representing the DRG (Diagnosis Related Group) assigned to the patient's hospital stay.

columns.name: DESCRIPTION
columns.description: Description of the DRG (Diagnosis Related Group).

columns.name: DRG_SEVERITY
columns.description: Severity level associated with the DRG (Diagnosis Related Group), which indicates the complexity or seriousness of the patient's condition.

columns.name: DRG_MORTALITY
columns.description: Mortality risk associated with the DRG (Diagnosis Related Group). Higher values indicate a greater risk of mortality for patients assigned to that DRG.

description: The ICUSTAYS table provides information on each patient's ICU stay within the MIMIC-III database. It links patients (`SUBJECT_ID`) to their hospital admissions (`HADM_ID`) and specific ICU stays (`ICUSTAY_ID`), including details about the database source (`DBSOURCE`), the first and last care units and wards the patient occupied, the admission and discharge times (`INTIME`, `OUTTIME`), and the length of stay (`LOS`). Each row represents a unique ICU stay.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the table.

columns.name: SUBJECT_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for a patient.

columns.name: HADM_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for a patient's hospital admission.

columns.name: ICUSTAY_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for a patient's stay in the ICU.

columns.name: DBSOURCE
columns.description: The database source where the data was originally recorded, such as 'carevue' or 'metavision'.

columns.name: FIRST_CAREUNIT
columns.description: The first care unit the patient was admitted to during their ICU stay (e.g., 'CSRU', 'MICU').

columns.name: LAST_CAREUNIT
columns.description: The last care unit the patient was in before discharge from the ICU (e.g., 'CSRU', 'MICU').

columns.name: FIRST_WARDID
columns.description: The ID of the first hospital ward the patient was admitted to.

columns.name: LAST_WARDID
columns.description: The ID of the last hospital ward the patient was in before discharge.

columns.name: INTIME
columns.description: The date and time the patient was admitted to the ICU.

columns.name: OUTTIME
columns.description: The date and time the patient was discharged from the ICU.

columns.name: LOS
columns.description: The length of stay in the ICU, in days.

description: The ADMISSIONS table contains information on hospital admissions for patients, including admission and discharge times, admission type and location, insurance details, demographic information (language, religion, marital status, ethnicity), diagnosis, and mortality status during the admission. It also includes flags indicating the presence of chartevent data for the admission. Each row represents a unique hospital admission.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the table.

columns.name: SUBJECT_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each patient.

columns.name: HADM_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each hospital admission.

columns.name: ADMITTIME
columns.description: Timestamp of when the patient was admitted to the hospital.

columns.name: DISCHTIME
columns.description: Timestamp of when the patient was discharged from the hospital.

columns.name: DEATHTIME
columns.description: Timestamp of when the patient died, if applicable. Null if the patient did not die during the hospital admission.

columns.name: ADMISSION_TYPE
columns.description: Type of admission, such as EMERGENCY, URGENT, or ELECTIVE.

columns.name: ADMISSION_LOCATION
columns.description: The location of the patient prior to admission to the hospital.

columns.name: DISCHARGE_LOCATION
columns.description: The location to which the patient was discharged after their hospital stay.

columns.name: INSURANCE
columns.description: The type of insurance the patient has.

columns.name: LANGUAGE
columns.description: The primary language spoken by the patient.

columns.name: RELIGION
columns.description: The patient's self-identified religion.

columns.name: MARITAL_STATUS
columns.description: The patient's marital status.

columns.name: ETHNICITY
columns.description: The patient's ethnicity.

columns.name: EDREGTIME
columns.description: Timestamp of when the patient was registered in the emergency department (ED).

columns.name: EDOUTTIME
columns.description: Timestamp of when the patient left the emergency department (ED).

columns.name: DIAGNOSIS
columns.description: The diagnosis given for the patient's admission.

columns.name: HOSPITAL_EXPIRE_FLAG
columns.description: A flag indicating whether the patient expired (died) during the hospital admission. 1 indicates the patient expired, 0 indicates the patient survived.

columns.name: HAS_CHARTEVENTS_DATA
columns.description: A flag indicating whether there is data for the patient in the CHARTEVENTS table. 1 indicates that chartevents data exists, 0 indicates that it does not.

description: The `D_ICD_DIAGNOSES` table provides a dictionary of ICD-9 diagnosis codes. It contains the ICD-9 code itself, along with short and long descriptive titles associated with each code. This table is useful for translating numeric ICD-9 codes into human-readable descriptions.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the dataset.

columns.name: ICD9_CODE
columns.description: ICD-9 code representing a diagnosis or procedure performed on a patient.

columns.name: SHORT_TITLE
columns.description: A short, descriptive title corresponding to the ICD-9 code. It provides a concise label for the diagnosis or procedure.

columns.name: LONG_TITLE
columns.description: A longer, more detailed title corresponding to the ICD-9 code, offering a comprehensive description of the diagnosis or procedure.

description: The `D_ITEMS` table provides a comprehensive dictionary of clinical measurements, lab events, and note types (ITEMIDs) used throughout the database. It includes detailed information about each ITEMID, such as its full text description (`LABEL`), abbreviation (`ABBREVIATION`), source database (`DBSOURCE`), the table it links to (`LINKSTO`), its category (`CATEGORY`), unit of measurement (`UNITNAME`), parameter type (`PARAM_TYPE`), and a (currently null) concept identifier (`CONCEPTID`). This table serves as a reference for understanding and interpreting data related to ITEMIDs in other tables.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the table.

columns.name: ITEMID
columns.description: Identifier for a clinical measurement, lab event, or note type.

columns.name: LABEL
columns.description: Full text description of the ITEMID (clinical measurement/note). More descriptive than ABBREVIATION.

columns.name: ABBREVIATION
columns.description: Abbreviated form of the LABEL, representing the clinical measurement/note.

columns.name: DBSOURCE
columns.description: Database from which the ITEMID originates, either 'carevue' or 'metavision'.

columns.name: LINKSTO
columns.description: Table that ITEMID refers to, e.g. 'chartevents', 'datetimeevents', etc.

columns.name: CATEGORY
columns.description: Category of the ITEMID, providing a further grouping for clinical measurements/notes.

columns.name: UNITNAME
columns.description: Unit of measurement associated with the ITEMID, such as 'mA', 'sec', or 'ml/min'.

columns.name: PARAM_TYPE
columns.description: Type of parameter associated with the ITEMID, such as 'Numeric with tag', 'Process', 'Checkbox', or 'Text'.

columns.name: CONCEPTID
columns.description: ID linking the ITEMID to a standardized concept, currently always null.

description: The `D_LABITEMS` table provides a dictionary of laboratory items, mapping internal `ITEMID` codes to descriptive information about each lab test. This includes the test's `LABEL`, the `FLUID` sampled, the `CATEGORY` of test, and the standardized `LOINC_CODE`. The table allows for easy interpretation of lab results stored using the `ITEMID`.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the dataset.

columns.name: ITEMID
columns.description: Identifier for a specific lab test. Links to the D_LABITEMS table.

columns.name: LABEL
columns.description: The plain text label or description of the lab test associated with ITEMID.

columns.name: FLUID
columns.description: The type of fluid that was sampled for the lab test.

columns.name: CATEGORY
columns.description: The broad category of the lab test performed (e.g., CHEMISTRY, BLOOD GAS).

columns.name: LOINC_CODE
columns.description: The LOINC code associated with the lab test, providing a standardized identifier.

description: The CAREGIVERS table contains information about caregivers, linking unique caregiver IDs (CGID) to job titles or roles. The table includes a shortened label for the role and a more detailed description. Each row is uniquely identified by ROW_ID.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the dataset.

columns.name: CGID
columns.description: Identifier for a caregiver.

columns.name: LABEL
columns.description: Shortened job title or category for a caregiver.

columns.name: DESCRIPTION
columns.description: Full job title or role description for a caregiver.

description: The PATIENTS table contains demographic and mortality information for patients within the dataset. It includes unique patient identifiers, gender, date of birth, and date of death information from various sources (hospital records, Social Security Administration). The table also includes an expire flag to indicate record status.

columns.name: ROW_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each row in the table.

columns.name: SUBJECT_ID
columns.description: Unique identifier for each patient in the dataset.

columns.name: GENDER
columns.description: Patient's gender, recorded as either 'F' (female) or 'M' (male).

columns.name: DOB
columns.description: Date of birth of the patient.

columns.name: DOD
columns.description: Date of death of the patient.

columns.name: DOD_HOSP
columns.description: Date of death recorded by the hospital.

columns.name: DOD_SSN
columns.description: Date of death recorded by the Social Security Administration.

columns.name: EXPIRE_FLAG
columns.description: Indicates whether the patient's record has expired. 0 indicates the record is active, 1 indicates the record is expired.
